text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker autotune roll, we see a 12-18% P99 spike on short-seq workloads (seqlen 32/64). Suspect warp/tile change + KV cache padding.
sam: which build/roll id?
maria: rolling: kernel-picker v2.3.1 (autotune-tiling) from canary, deploy ~22:10 UTC. thread_ts: 1862500000
jake: saw the perfbot alert. Can you paste a perf trace or flame?
maria: quick top-of-stack from perfbot:
perf-bot: profiling output: total tokens/sec drop from 52k -> 45k on g4dn. Top hotspots: softmax, matmul_16x64_tileB, kv_update.
maria: attaching snippet:
```text
kernel matmul_16x64_tileB launch=(256,1,1) sm=48 reg=64 time=1.8ms
kernel matmul_8x128_tileA launch=(128,1,1) sm=32 reg=80 time=2.4ms
kv_prefetch time=0.4ms increased by 3x (seq32)
```
priya: interesting — autotuner bumped tileB sizes to favor long-seq throughput; short-seq overhead from register spilling? reg=80 looks high.
sam: check occupancy numbers — more registers => fewer warps => P99 climb. classic tradeoff.
jake: I ran a local microbench: toggling warp_specialization=true drops P99 by ~9% for seq32 synthetic runs.
maria: did the tuner log how it trades off occupancy vs smem? I don't think it considers sequence-length distribution skew in the objective.
sam: current autotune objective: maximize aggregate throughput across sampled seq histogram. It's a weighted avg using sampled distribution but doesn't model KV-cache miss amplification on short prefixes.
perf-bot: autotune run id: atune_20260316_1876 selected tileB=16x64 for arch=sm86; objective_score=0.87 on sampled hist mean=512.
priya: suggestion: add two-mode policy — short-path (<128) picks a kernel with smaller reg footprint, long-path keeps current choice. Also consider prefix-KV padding for warp alignment to avoid thrash.
jake: agreed. Also propose a cheap runtime sampling: seqlen peek -> route to short/long kernel choice (cost <50us) so we don't always pay long-path tax.
maria: any risks from maintaining separate picks? code complexity / kernel explosion?
sam: keep one codegen but param-driven launch config (tile hints) so we don't duplicate full kernels. runtime decides tile_dim_hint and launch params.
priya: profiling note — when register pressure >64 on sm86 occupancy drops to ~0.375 -> p99 increases nonlinearly. We should encode occupancy floors into tuner penalty.
maria: can someone produce a small repro with seq32/64 showing kv_prefetch blowup and kernel timings? I'll file a regression.
jake: I'll run a synthetic workload on dedicated pool with -runs=1000 and collect nvprof + perf counters. ping me in 30m and I'll paste logs.
perf-bot: lowered autotuner sampling variance in CI to avoid noisy medians; new config committed to /configs/atune/seq_mode.yaml (roll in staging).
maria: follow-ups: (1) add kernel selection short/long class in runtime, (2) upstream autotuner objective tweak to penalize short-p99 regressions, (3) add kv prefetch backpressure for tiny batches + pad-to-warp option.
priya: I'll draft a short spec and test plan (unit perf tests + canary checklist). Keep it minimal: three config flags + microbench harness.
sam: created ticket INF-778 and assigned to eng-runtime (prio P1). :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — keep updates here.
